product.name: Greer
product.description: Open-source, self-hostable tool that helps small or new SaaS builders create a genuine community and get feedback on their product. It finds conversations where the builder can genuinely help and gives them short reply ideas (never AI-written replies).

cases.title: Ask HN: One month, zero paying customers – keep it or kill it?
cases.text:
When I created the site scanmypage.com, I genuinely believed that many business owners would use it — especially because of the price: just $1 for a website analysis.

Analytics — 
Google Search Console — 
Still struggling to gain good visibility on Google.

I then started paying for Google Ads — 
Built and optimized what I believe is a solid campaign —

But now a month has passed, and the site still hasn’t generated a single paying customer.

So my question is: What would you do?

Would you keep the site alive and continue improving and marketing it, or would you kill it, accept that the idea isn’t gaining traction, and move on to the next project?

Keep it or kill it?

cases.title: Go Concurrency Distilled
cases.text:
I agree with everything you're saying. I think it comes down to design philosophy. Erlang's ecosystem is well tuned for building fault tolerant systems and features concurrency heavily to solve for that. Go is for general purpose programming in big organizations with massive variance in developer experience that has concurrency as a first class concept for the ability to scale (among other things).

Of course, in some sense fault tolerance and scaling are two sides of the same coin. They're both measures of availability. They're just different approaches to that.

cases.title: Xfinity silently blocks lots of new domains
cases.text:
We built a site for a launch and it was unreachable for anyone on an Xfinity router. We only found out because we have an Xfinity router at home. There's no notice to the site owner.

Xfinity's Advanced Security draws on third-party domain reputation lists and blocks at the gateway. We found out a blacklist called SURBL had flagged us. Not sure exactly what tripped it. Since then I've hit the same block on 10+ unrelated sites and told the site owner. Now sharing with everyone here.

How to check whether it's happening to you:

https://spa.xfinity.com/check_url_status
If blocked, look for the upstream list: https://mxtoolbox.com/blacklists.aspx
